title: If We Had to Make $1M Fast, We’d Start These Businesses
channel: Chris Koerner on The Koerner Office Podcast
promo_conflict: Chris uses his own AI voice-agent screen-recording demo and a paying prospect as promotional proof; no paid sponsorship is stated.

stated_problem.quote: Small businesses are overwhelmed. They don't really know what to do with AI, but they want results, right?
stated_problem.speaker: Chris Koerner

idea.name: Plug-and-play AI automation agency
idea.one_liner: Install specific AI workflows, such as after-hours call answering and missed-call follow-up, for small businesses in exchange for setup fees and retainers.
idea.customer: Small businesses, including home-service companies such as garage-door repair firms
idea.offer: Niche-specific AI automations that capture missed leads or save time
idea.revenue_model: Setup fee, monthly retainer, or payment per closed lead

key_quotes.quote: Automating missed call follow-up texts for any any home services company, and you recover 15% of leads.
I created an AI voice agent with literally like six clicks.

claims.claim: A business owner agreed to pay 57 minutes after the demonstration.
claims.quote: 57 minutes later, I had a business owner that said, "Yes, I want to pay for your service."

claims.claim: A missed-call follow-up workflow could recover 15% of leads.
claims.quote: Automating missed call follow-up texts for any any home services company, and you recover 15% of leads.

claims.claim: Garage-door repair jobs can be worth $500 to $3,000.
claims.quote: And I just used Chachet to make a a knowledge base that said, you know, you are a 24/7 answering service for a garage door repair company because I chose that industry because it's higher ticket, $500 to $3,000 per job.

claims.claim: A business could pay $100 per month for AI phone answering, or pay per lead.
claims.quote: You can't afford a full-time employee after hours to answer the phone, but you can definitely pay $100 a month and have AI available at any moment or pay per lead.

claims.claim: The proposed setup charge is $3,000, plus a monthly retainer and possible upsells.
claims.quote: I'd reach out to a lot of owners. I'd close clients and free charge 3,000 for a setup, have a monthly retainer, and then maybe we do some upsells in there.

claims.claim: The speaker cites 32 million small businesses in America.
claims.quote: There are 32 million small businesses in America alone.

acquisition_channels.details: Scraped garage-door repair companies in DFW and texted them.

ideas.delivery: Configure and install voice agents and follow-up workflows, then provide ongoing support; the business owner handles calls through the AI system.

uk_legal_risk.reason: The demonstrated customer acquisition uses unsolicited texts to scraped repair firms, which may include sole traders; UK PECR bars unsolicited marketing texts to sole traders and individuals. Follow-up texts to consumers also need an appropriate basis and consent where they are marketing.

ideas.other_uk_rules: UK GDPR applies to caller and lead data; call recording needs suitable notices and a lawful basis. PECR rules also apply to electronic marketing.
